steps.prompt: Is this a deep, gaping, or heavily bleeding wound? If so, move to the Severe Bleeding guide instead.
This needs more than minor wound care. Apply firm pressure and call emergency services or go to an emergency department.
Apply gentle pressure with a clean cloth or gauze for a few minutes to stop bleeding. Elevate the injured area above the level of the heart if possible.
Rinse the wound gently under clean running water for several minutes to remove dirt and debris. Do not scrub.
Pat dry with a clean cloth. Apply an antiseptic if available, then cover with a sterile adhesive dressing or bandage.
Was the wound caused by an animal bite, dirty object (rusty nail, soil), or is there any sign of infection (increasing redness, pus, swelling, warmth)?
Seek medical care to assess the need for tetanus booster, antibiotics, or wound closure. Animal bites also need evaluation for infection risk.
Change the dressing daily or if wet/soiled. Seek care if the wound does not begin to close, becomes red or swollen, or you are unsure about tetanus status.
